Being one who travels a lot for mini vacations, I get lots of Choice Hotel points.

There is definitely overlap between brands. Quality Inn is usually the older/converted hotel while Comfort Inns are almost always built ground up as those.

What is interesting is the level of the hotel doesn’t really directly influence the quality of the included breakfast. My best breakfast I’ve had in the chain was a converted Quality Inns in the middle of nowhere Pennsylvania. While one of nicer convention hotels in Minneapolis’s downtown had just toast and cereal on a breakfast buffet that was smaller than the kitchen countertop in my own house.

I usually agree in that the location and price tend to be most important. If I'm in a good location, I'll spend even less time at the hotel. Why spend more for that?

But there's some occassions where a nicer hotel is really worth it. Like, for a trip you wanna be romantic, it can set the mood. Remote work or cold winter weather can keep me indoors more. And perks like a gym or pool (and a proper one at that) can be really nice.

But yeah, for most travel, the hotel doesn't matter and isn't the point. But I think that's also kinda what the hotel chains are going for with having so many brands. They're covering every use case and preference.
